title: Pair That Hits the Target
statement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, find the two different positions i and j whose values add up to target.

Exactly one such pair exists. You may not use the same position twice, but two positions may hold equal values.

Return the two indexes as [i, j] with i < j.

examples.why: The two 6s are at different positions, so they form a valid pair.
4 + 4 would be 8, but there is only one 4 and a position cannot be used twice. The answer is 1 + 7.

constraints: Exactly one pair of positions adds up to target
hints: For each value x, you already know exactly which other value you need. What is it?
Checking every later element for that partner is O(n²). What structure finds a value instantly?
Walk left to right with a map from value to index. For each x, look up target − x among the values you have already passed, then store x.

explain.intuition:
Once you fix one number x, the other one is decided: it must be target − x, its complement. So the question for each element becomes "have I already seen my complement?", which a hash map answers in O(1).

Checking the map before inserting the current element is what stops a position from pairing with itself, and it also handles equal values: the first 6 is in the map when the second 6 arrives.
steps: Create an empty map from value to the index where it appeared.
For each index j with value x: compute need = target − x.
If need is in the map at index i, return [i, j]. Since i was stored earlier, i < j automatically.
pitfalls: Inserting all values into the map first and then searching: [4, 1, 7] with target 8 would pair 4 with itself unless you also check that the indexes differ.
Sorting the values and using two pointers loses the original indexes. Sort pairs of (value, index) instead, and return the indexes in increasing order.

solutions.title: Try every pair
solutions.idea: Two nested loops over i < j. Clear, but quadratic.

solutions.title: Sort indexes, then two pointers
solutions.idea: Sort the positions by value. A pointer at each end moves inward: too small a sum moves the left pointer up, too big moves the right one down.

solutions.title: One pass with a complement map
solutions.idea: For each value, look up its complement among the values already passed, then remember the value.

followups: The array is already sorted. Can you do it with O(1) extra memory?
Return every pair of values that adds to target, without repeating the same pair of values.
